reader:
The specimen ontology's rules about reading a label; transcribe the label exactly as written all the same:
- A numeric date whose day-month and month-day orders give two different dates is either until evidence decides: never read it one way alone.
- A code is never a date nor part of one: a slide code such as "IV-29-68-4" beside the collecting date "IV-23-48" is no date.
- A label's type (locality, determination, code) never limits what its text holds: a determination label may write a locality.
- Keep an elevation's foot mark (') or "ft" wherever it is written; a number's size alone never makes it feet.
- Precise Location is the label's locality as written: every line of its locality text, with its line breaks, the higher places and an elevation written on those lines, never a collector or a date; never only its first line, and a locality naming nothing finer than its town has one too.

organiser:
The specimen ontology's rules:
- A specimen has one collecting event: where two labels write two different collecting dates, or two place names no source confirms as one place, give both texts, never one label's alone.
- A place below the country lies inside the country and province its label writes.
- The places form one chain, country > province or state > county > city, each inside the one above it.
- The collecting date is on or before the determination date, the same day allowed; dates written at different precisions agree on the parts both write.
- A numeric date whose day-month and month-day orders give two different dates is either until evidence decides: never read it one way alone.
- A code is never a date nor part of one: a slide code such as "IV-29-68-4" beside the collecting date "IV-23-48" is no date.
- A label's type (locality, determination, code) never limits what its text holds: a determination label may write a locality.
- Keep an elevation's foot mark (') or "ft" wherever it is written; a number's size alone never makes it feet.
- Never give an elevation a unit its label does not write: not from its size, the place or a map.
- An elevation's written unit decides its field: metres go to the metre fields, feet to the foot fields.
- Leave a larger place the label does not write empty: never take it from a smaller place's parents.
- Never convert an elevation to the other unit: give it in the unit the label writes.
- Give Date Visited To only from an end date the label writes, never from a single collecting date.
- Precise Location is the label's locality as written: every line of its locality text, with its line breaks, the higher places and an elevation written on those lines, never a collector or a date; never only its first line, and a locality naming nothing finer than its town has one too.
- A name GBIF finds only outside class Insecta, the collection's higher taxon, such as a mammal's or a bird's genus written with no host marker, is never the specimen's taxon; when the labels write no other name, the specimen's taxon is not on the label.
- A name after a host marker on its line ("Host Thomomys", "Ex. Canis familiaris", "from nest of Formica rufa") is never the specimen's taxon; when the labels write no other name, the specimen's taxon is not on the label.
- Where this field's parts are written on different labels (the genus on one label and the species on another; the day and month on one, the year on another), answer several_possibilities with each label's part, copied exactly, as an option, and say in the explanation what each label writes ("label 1 writes genus Aus; label 2 writes species bus"); never join the parts into one literal, and never answer one part as the whole value.
